passages.context: Westcott's notes on the seeing verbs at John 20:5 and 20:6, and Arthur Westcott's editorial footnote recording his father's marginal notes and private letter, read on printed page 339 rendered from the hashed facsimile.
passages.notes: The printing sets the Greek verbs blepei and theorei and the participle entetyligmenon in Greek type within these notes; they are omitted from the transcription, which carries no Greek, and the omissions are marked by the surrounding wording. The last two transcribed lines are Arthur Westcott's editorial footnote, signed A. W. in the printing, and record his father's later opinions; they are not Bishop Westcott's own printed notes.

passages.context: Westcott's notes on the phrase apart wrapped up into one place and on he saw and believed, read on printed page 340 rendered from the hashed facsimile, with the Greek text of John 20:6-10 printed above the notes on the same page.
passages.notes: The lemma of the first note is the Greek phrase for apart wrapped up into one place, followed by the Vulgate's separatim involutum in unum locum; the Greek lemma is omitted from this transcription because the record carries no Greek type. The square brackets in the first transcribed line are Westcott's own. The second and third lines belong to the note on believed, whose opening clause The exact interpretation of the word believed is difficult stands earlier on the same page and is not transcribed.

work.author: Brooke Foss Westcott
work.description: Westcott's commentary on the Fourth Gospel, printing the Greek text with a facing English column and notes. Published posthumously in two volumes in 1908 by his son Arthur Westcott, who added editorial footnotes recording his father's later marginal notes and a private letter. The notes on John 20:5-10 stand at volume 2, pages 339 to 341. A locus is the Gospel chapter.
